decks.notes: The deck focuses on using Paradoxical Outcome to generate huge amounts of mana and draw cards by bouncing Coveted Jewel and other artifacts. It also utilizes artifact mana acceleration like Grim Monolith and Moxen to power out big plays, while also utilizing control elements like Force of Will and Sink into Stupor to disrupt opponents. The deck aims to ultimately assemble a powerful combo involving Time Vault and Voltaic Key to take infinite turns and lock the opponent out of the game, with additional win conditions like Tinker for Karn, the Great Creator or Urza's Saga for extra versatility.

This deck aims to utilize the powerful card advantage of Paradoxical Outcome to generate a large amount of mana and draw through the deck quickly. By combining fast mana sources like Moxen and Black Lotus with artifacts that generate additional mana or cards like Tolarian Academy and Urza's Saga, the deck can set up a game-winning combo involving Time Vault and Key. The inclusion of Force of Will and other interaction helps protect the combo, while Lurrus of the Dream-Den provides additional value and recursion. The deck's strategy hinges on assembling the combo pieces quickly and efficiently to win the game before the opponent can respond.

The deck focuses on utilizing artifacts and artifacts matter cards to create a fast and disruptive aggressive strategy. By leveraging powerful artifacts like Mishra's Workshop, Moxen, and Crucible of Worlds, the deck aims to generate mana quickly and play threats ahead of curve. Additionally, cards like Trinisphere, Nettlecyst, and Sphere of Resistance help to disrupt opponents' game plans and slow them down, allowing the deck to get ahead and overwhelm them with a combination of efficient threats and resource denial.

The deck focuses on utilizing the powerful card Underworld Breach to create a combo win condition. It includes various powerful combo pieces such as Black Lotus, Bolas's Citadel, and Brain Freeze, along with cards to help find and protect the combo like Demonic Tutor, Force of Will, and Vampiric Tutor. The deck aims to quickly assemble its combo pieces, generate a large amount of mana, and use Underworld Breach to repeatedly cast cards from the graveyard to either mill the opponent's library or deal lethal damage in a single turn.

This deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy while maintaining control through counterspells and removal spells. It aims to out-value the opponent by utilizing powerful card draw spells and versatile creatures. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional resilience and recursion options. The deck also features a mix of efficient removal, card filtering, and disruptive elements to ensure it can adapt to different matchups and assert dominance in the mid to late game.

The deck focuses on quickly ramping out threats like Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Hollow One while disrupting the opponent with taxing artifacts like Sphere of Resistance and Thorn of Amethyst. It also utilizes Crucible of Worlds with Wasteland and Strip Mine to control the opponent's mana base. Additionally, the deck can use Karn, the Great Creator to shut down artifacts or search for specific answers from the sideboard, showcasing a strong aggro strategy with MUD elements.

The deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan by using hatebears like Anointed Peacekeeper, Archon of Emeria, and Chancellor of the Annex, while also utilizing aggro creatures like Seasoned Dungeoneer and White Plume Adventurer to apply pressure. It also includes disruptive elements like Wasteland, Trinisphere, and Chalice of the Void to hinder the opponent's strategy. The deck aims to control the game through its disruptive creatures and spells, while also attacking aggressively to quickly close out the game.

The deck focuses on quickly playing powerful artifacts such as Mana Crypt, Black Lotus, and Moxen to generate mana and accelerate into game-changing threats like Karn, the Great Creator and Mystic Forge. Using cards like Sensei's Divining Top and Nettlecyst to control the board and protect key pieces, the deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with aggressive artifact creatures like Glaring Fleshraker and Scrawling Crawler. With efficient mana sources like Mishra's Workshop and Ancient Tomb, the deck can deploy threats quickly and disrupt the opponent's strategy with cards like Lodestone Golem and Strip Mine.

This deck focuses on using disruptive spells and creatures to disrupt the opponent's game plan while gaining card advantage through efficient draw spells. It also utilizes synergies with graveyard recursion and mana denial to control the pace of the game, preventing the opponent from setting up their strategy effectively. The deck aims to apply constant pressure and keep the opponent on the back foot, utilizing a mix of creature removal, counterspells, and disruptive creatures to establish dominance on the battlefield.

The focus of this deck is to disrupt the opponent's game plan by using hatebears and aggro creatures while also utilizing powerful mana acceleration to quickly establish a dominant board presence. By restricting the opponent's options with cards like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex, this deck aims to overwhelm them with efficient threats and disruption. The combination of hatebears, mana acceleration, and disruptive elements creates a game plan that punishes slower or less interactive strategies, allowing the deck to seize control of the game and dictate the pace of play.

The deck focuses on utilizing powerful mana accelerants and card draw spells to quickly assemble the Coveted Jewel combo. By generating a large amount of mana with cards like Mishra's Workshop and Grim Monolith, the deck can play and activate the Coveted Jewel to generate card advantage and further accelerate its game plan. Additionally, the deck includes disruptive elements like Force of Will and Tinker to protect the combo, while also featuring key cards like Time Vault and Mystic Forge to further enhance its strategy.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy while using efficient card draw and graveyard recursion to maintain card advantage. It includes a mix of counterspells, removal spells, and powerful card draw cards. The companion card Lurrus of the Dream-Den allows for additional value by recurring low-cost permanents from the graveyard. With a strong mana base and a focus on controlling the game tempo, this Dimir Control deck aims to outvalue and outmaneuver the opponent through attrition and precise decision-making.

The primary focus of this deck is to maintain control over the game by using counterspells, removal, and card draw to disrupt the opponent's strategy. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional card advantage and recurring threats. The deck utilizes a combination of efficient threats like Orcish Bowmasters and Psychic Frog, along with powerful spells like Ancestral Recall and Demonic Tutor, to outvalue and outmaneuver the opponent. The mana base is streamlined with fetch lands and dual lands, ensuring consistency in casting spells while also disrupting the opponent's mana base with cards like Wasteland and Strip Mine.

This Vintage 1 vs 1 deck focuses on utilizing a combination of fast mana accelerants and tutoring spells to assemble the necessary pieces for a lethal Tendrils of Agony combo. The deck includes various ways to generate mana quickly, like Lotus Petal and the Moxen, as well as card draw and filtering spells to help find key combo pieces. By efficiently casting spells and generating storm count, the deck aims to cast Tendrils of Agony with a high storm count, allowing for a devastating finish to the game.

The deck focuses on utilizing Paradoxical Outcome to generate a large amount of mana and draw cards in order to set up a powerful combo win condition. It includes powerful cards such as Ancestral Recall and Time Walk to gain card advantage and extra turns, as well as counterspells like Force of Will to protect the combo. The addition of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion adds an extra layer of resilience and recursion to the deck, making it a strong and versatile choice for Vintage 1 vs 1 play.

The deck focuses on a proactive strategy that combines aggressive creatures with disruptive elements (hatebears) to slow down the opponent. It aims to control the game by limiting the opponent's options while applying pressure with efficient creatures. The deck includes powerful hate cards like Chancellor of the Annex and Archon of Emeria to disrupt the opponent's game plan, while also utilizing cards like Swords to Plowshares and Solitude for removal. The presence of mana acceleration and card draw engines like Seasoned Dungeoneer and Witch Enchanter helps the deck maintain its momentum and outvalue the opponent.
